"Instead of disposing of prunings from your winter garden work through burning or shredding, consider repurposing them into a dead hedge. This dead hedge can serve as a fantastic windbreak, provide a sanctuary for wildlife, and help divide different areas of your garden. Begin by placing stakes or old fence posts in two rows that are 50cm apart, then fill the space in between with the prunings, ensuring to place larger branches at the base for stability. Over time, the material will settle into place, creating a natural and sustainable barrier. 

If you're looking to treat yourself after the holiday season, why not pre-order a copy of 'The Book Of Seeds' by Paul Smith? This beautifully illustrated guide showcases 600 of the most unique and stunning plant species from around the world, making it a perfect addition to any botanical lover's collection.

For a burst of color in your winter garden, consider planting winter-flowering clematis varieties like 'Advent Bells' or 'Jingle Bells' in a sunny and sheltered spot. These plants will reward you with fragrant, creamy blooms from December to February.

Is there anything else I can help with?".
